clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old Caucasian female nonsmoker presented to the emergency department with 4 months of progressive dyspnea and back pain, having been previously misdiagnosed with pneumonia at an outside facility based on imaging showing right upper lobe consolidation. On admission, CT chest revealed near-complete right upper lobe collapse with consolidation and mediastinal lymphadenopathy (E001), MRI spine demonstrated a C7 50% compression fracture with widespread lytic lesions concerning for metastatic disease (E002), and CT abdomen identified a 15-mm hypodense liver nodule (E003). Initial transthoracic biopsy of the right upper lobe was non-diagnostic, showing only fibrous pleural tissue and lymphocytic infiltrate without malignant cells (E004). Subsequent fluoroscopy-guided liver biopsy of the metastatic lesion demonstrated a malignant undifferentiated neoplasm with epithelioid morphology, nests and cords in hyalinized sclerotic stroma, eosinophilic cytoplasm, and round-to-ovoid nuclei (E006). Immunohistochemical staining revealed strong MUC4 positivity with negative staining for claudin-4, ERG, CD31, CAMTA1, P40, ETV-4, and NUT, with preserved BRG1 and INI1 nuclear staining (E008), leading to the explicit conclusion of sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (E008). First-line chemotherapy with doxorubicin was initiated (E010).
